thread:
marta: Quick ping — noticed a cluster of correctable ECC + a couple Xid bursts in eu-central racks 11-14 around 01:42 UTC. Heatmap shows concentrated activity not global. Anyone seeing network noise or kernel restarts?
sam: seeing same. correctable ECC rate spikes on those racks, uncorrectable still low but Xid bursts look correlated to iface errors on the top-of-rack switches.
riley: thx. Can you paste the per-rack PromQL? I want to normalise by active card-hours to avoid short-lived VM bias.
marta: use this as a starter (per-rack, per-10k-card-hours):
```
(sum(increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1h])) by (rack)
/ (sum(increase(gpu_card_active_seconds[1h])) by (rack) / 3600)) * 10000
```
sam: nice. also track uncorrectable separately: `increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_total[6h]) by (gpu_card)` — those are the hard failures.
chen: operational note 12: our current ejection policy is binary: single Xid -> eject. That triggers a hard replace which is expensive (avg replacement 45m + job restarts). We should consider multi-stage ejection.
riley: propose "graded ejection" flow: soft-mark -> attempt warm-reboot -> isolate (no new pods) -> hard-eject if persistent. Soft-mark threshold = transient-correctable burn rate; hard-eject thresholds = sustained uncorrectable or 3 Xid events in 24h.
marta: agree. Dashboard panels to build: per-rack normalized correctable / 10k card-hours, uncorrectable count (24h), Xid burst heatmap, iface_errors overlay, per-rack boot/reboot events, and a churn panel (reboots vs permanent replacements).
sam: suggested SLOs (provisional): p95 correctable < 1.0 / 10k card-hours; p99 uncorrectable < 0.05 / 10k card-hours. Mitigation burn-rate: 2x over 1h to enter soft-mark.
chen: let's also compute a rack health index: 0-100 score = 100 - clamp( (w1 * normalized_correctable) + (w2 * uncorrectable_count) + (w3 * churn_rate) , 0, 100 ). Use decay window 24h and weights w1=0.6, w2=1.8, w3=0.5 as a start. We'll iterate.
marta: want an alert when rack health index < 70 or when capacity loss in rack > 3% in 10m. That should prevent unnoticed degradation.
riley: I'll run a simulation to compare current binary-eject vs graded-eject on last 6 months of telemetry. Key metrics: replacements per event, mean time to recovery, and job restart impact. Expect graded flow to cut permanent replacements by ~30-40% on intermittent events.
sam: add a panel for "soft-mark -> recovery ratio" and a metric `soft_mark_successes / soft_marks_total` over 24h. That will help tune warm-reboot attempts vs immediate eject.
infra-bot: Incident INC-4927 created for eu-central GPU anomaly; correlated signals: network.iface_tx_errors and kernel.nodemgr_restarts. Assigned eng-infra.
chen: micro-ops: implement soft-mark label on nodes (kube annotate + metric), block new scheduling to the card, trigger a 10m warm-reboot job, if metric returns to baseline mark recovered, else escalate to isolate then hard-eject.
marta: I'll build the Grafana JSON with the new panels and wire the rack health index gauge. Will PR into ops-dashboards and link here.
riley: after sims I'll post expected cost delta (replacement minutes saved, provisioning cost) and a short runbook change proposal for #eng-oncall.
sam: once dashboard is live we should run a 2-week shadow mode: compute alerts but don't auto-eject. Use shadow data to tune thresholds.
marta: agreed. Thanks all — this thread captures proposal: per-rack normalized metrics, graded ejection flow, rack health index + specific provisional SLOs and next steps (simulate, dashboard JSON, shadow run).
